instructions: Cut the hard core out of the top of each tomato, then slice the 1.5 lbs tomatoes into rounds about 1/4 inch thick.
Drain the 16 oz mozzarella, pat it dry with paper towel and slice it about 1/4 inch thick.
Pick a big handful of leaves off the basil, about 1/3 cup, and leave them whole.
On a large platter, overlap the tomato and mozzarella slices in rows, tucking a basil leaf in between every few slices.
Right before you serve it, sprinkle the 1/2 tsp salt and the 1/4 tsp pepper over the platter and drizzle the 3 tbsp olive oil all over. Salt it at the last minute, or the tomatoes will turn watery.
Drizzle the 2 tbsp balsamic glaze over the top, or leave it off for the plain version.
method_notes: All three layer ripe tomatoes, fresh mozzarella and whole or torn basil and finish with extra virgin olive oil, salt and pepper. Natasha's Kitchen (the lead) slices both about 1/4 inch thick, tucks basil between the slices on a platter, seasons only right before serving and adds balsamic glaze as an option. RecipeTin Eats tosses halved cherry tomatoes and bocconcini in a garlic, mustard and white wine vinegar dressing with dried herbs, then drizzles balsamic glaze. Grantourismo keeps it to bocconcini, cherry tomatoes, basil, oil, salt and pepper. This one follows the lead's amounts as a lunch for 4 with bread on the side.
